relations.subject: tool:couchbase-server
relations.evidence: The `couchbase-server` command is used to control aspects of a Couchbase Server that has been installed, on a supported Linux platform, by means of the _non-root_ procedure; as described in [Non-Root Install and Upgrade](../install/non-root.md).

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-server
relations.evidence: This command _cannot_ be used to control a Couchbase Server installed by the standard, package-based install procedure.

notable_absence.finding: No Couchbase RBAC role or privilege is mentioned anywhere on this page - only OS-level context (which Linux user installed the server). That is arguably correct here since the tool operates below the RBAC layer entirely (it starts/stops a daemon, before any cluster credentials apply), but it is worth flagging alongside cbepctl-intro.md and cbstats-intro.md's identical silence, since together all three raise the same absence across this batch. Separately: the '--version' example output is 'Couchbase Server 6.6.0-7853 (EE)' - a stale, pre-7.0 example version left unchanged in the 8.0 tree, consistent with this round's authorship-provenance hypothesis of lighter editorial refresh on cli/ pages.

cross_component_finding: The page links out to two install-tree pages (Install Couchbase Server on Linux, Non-Root Install and Upgrade) for the two install modes it distinguishes, but neither install-tree page is in this batch, so the install: concepts minted here are unverified beyond this single page's own framing.
